note: The paper argues that AI is becoming embedded in university teaching, learning, support and administration, and that institutions must address adoption challenges to shape how higher education evolves, which matters to anyone tracking AI's growing role in education.
title: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence on teaching and learning in higher education

reading.body:
A 2017 paper on AI in higher education has accumulated 1,937 citations, which makes it one of the most-cited framings of the subject even though it reports no experimental results.

The paper's claim is that AI is spreading across teaching, learning, student support, and administration at once, not arriving as a single tool in a single department. Its contribution is a research agenda and a list of adoption challenges, not findings. The citation count is the signal here: a framing paper published in 2017 became a standard reference for a field that grew after it.

For AI specifically, the argument locates the pressure inside institutions rather than inside models. Universities adopting AI across four functions at once face coordination and governance problems, and the paper says those choices will shape what higher education becomes. That is a claim about organizations, not about compute, buildings, or power, and the data offers no basis for connecting it to any of them.

What the data does not cover is large. There is no information on which institutions adopted what, no measurement of adoption rates, no outcome for students, and no update since 2017. The citation count shows influence, not correctness, and a paper can be cited heavily for posing a question that later work answers differently.

explain_beginner: This paper looks at how artificial intelligence is starting to appear in universities, not just in one area but across teaching, learning, student support, and administration. The authors ask what this means for how students learn and how universities operate and change over time. They note that new technology is arriving quickly and being adopted faster than before. The main point is that universities face real challenges in adopting AI well, and that these choices will shape what higher education becomes. This matters because AI is becoming a normal part of university life.
explain_business: For executives, this paper signals that artificial intelligence is spreading through universities in teaching, learning, student support, and administration, and that adoption is speeding up. The authors argue that institutions must actively address the challenges of adopting these technologies, because those choices will influence how higher education develops. In practice, this means leaders should treat AI adoption as a strategic issue that touches many parts of the institution, not a single department's project. The decision it informs is whether and how to plan for AI adoption deliberately, so the institution helps shape its future rather than reacting to it.
explain_practitioner: The authors examine the emergence of artificial intelligence in higher education and its educational implications for student learning and institutional teaching and evolution. They consider recent technological advances and the accelerating adoption of new technologies in universities, then use these trends to anticipate the future character of higher education where AI is embedded throughout the institution. The paper identifies challenges that institutions and student learning face when adopting these technologies across teaching, learning, student support, and administration, and it outlines directions for further research. The key contribution is framing adoption challenges and a research agenda rather than reporting experimental results.
